   MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 6, 2019
(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:
The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, February 6, 2019, in the Community
Room, on the first floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge of
Allegiance by Sharon Mann-Garrett, Economic Development Manager,
the meeting was called to order at 5:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:
Present:  Commissioner Erick Holly
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aide’ Trejo
  Acting Chairman Terry Coleman
Excused
Absence:  Chairman Larry Spring

Staff:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Jeff Lewis, Assistant City Attorney
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Fred Jackson, Senior Planner
  Bernard McCrumby, Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner
  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., Director of E.C.D.
  Sharon Mann-Garrett, Manager of E.D.
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:
Ms. Wilcox stated that Item 5a is being pulled from tonight’s PC
meeting, and will be re-noticed at a later date.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

None.

(5) PUBLIC HEARING:

5A. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2018-014(SP-2018-014) AT 330 EAST
MANCHESTER BOULEVARD. A public hearing to consider an application
by Aria Shafiee, representing 330 Manchester Management LLC, for
Special Use Permit No. 2018-014 (SP-2018-014) to allow the retail
sale of beer and wine for off-site consumption in a proposed
convenience market on a 55,315 square-foot HC (Historic Core) zoned
property at 330 East Manchester Boulevard. This item has been
pulled and will be re-noticed.

5B. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2018-008 (SP-2018-008) AT 532 WEST
MANCHESTER BOULEVARD. A public hearing to consider an application
by Cole Feyijimi to appeal the denial of a Sign Adjustment No.
2018-008 (SA-2018-008) to legalize a previously installed
approximately 48 square-foot internally-illuminated bi-faced LED
sign for the display of on-site advertising only, C-2 (General
Commercial) zoned property at 532 West Manchester Boulevard.

Mr. Bernard McCrumby, Planner made the staff presentation.

Acting Chairman Coleman asked the Planning Commission if there
were any questions for staff.
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 6, 2019
Commissioner Rice asked:
 Is there any reason the sign is not currently illuminated, nor
  has not been on since its installation as it appears to be
  operational?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that there was a mandate from Code
  Enforcement to the owner to have the sign turned off until
  the appropriate approvals are obtained.
 Have you personally had the opportunity to see the sign
  illuminated?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated no he has not.

Commissioner Trejo asked:
 What type of sign is it, an electronic sign?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated it is an electronic LED sign that would
  display general information regarding the business, also
  showing services that are provided at the subject site, as
  well as any types of listings the applicant may have for
  purchase here in the City of Inglewood or beyond.
 Was the sign installed illegally?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated yes, but to better clarify the situation,
  the applicant had a previous pole sign approved that would
  allow for a small strip LED sign to give the date,
  temperature, time of day, along with a flat-panel raceway
  pole sign above that which gave the name of the business,
  hours of operation and location. What the applicant did was
  switch the size of the signs and they’re location on the pole.
  The small LED strip which originally gave a line of text has
  now been increased in size to give a full LED Animated Display
  to show properties available for purchase as well as listings
  already sold, with services provided in large LED Lettering.
 Was it Code Enforcement that was made aware of this?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated yes, actually it was the applicant who
  once was cited by Code Enforcement, came into the City’s
  planning office to find out how he could have the new sign
  approved and obtain a permit for the sign design and layout,
  and that was when he was informed that this type of signage
  is not approved here in Inglewood and that he would have to
  apply for a Sign Adjustment. Now the actual area of the pole
  sign was not increased, just the size of the LED sign was
  increased to become larger while the flat-panel raceway sign
  became smaller, which was the catalyst that required the
  applicant to apply for the Sign Adjustment.
 So to be clear, the actual size of the sign did not increase,
  but the switching to the larger LED sign was the key?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated yes, the actual larger LED sign with
  displayed images is not allowed per the Inglewood Municipal
  Code without a sign adjustment permit and what is allowed per
  the code is electronic signs with text of time, hours of
  operation, information of services, and date.
 So if it is approved, by the display the darkened area would be
  what is being shown right now, but if it is not approved,
  although the sign size remains the same the applicant will have
  to change what is being displayed?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that the applicant will have the option
  to go back to what was originally approved and permitted,
  which was the flat-panel raceway pole sign and or they would
  just be able to only display time, temperature and date. No
  images of any sort would be allowed.

  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 6, 2019
Acting Chairman Coleman asked:
 When Code Enforcement went out to cite the applicant, what
  caught their attention, was the sign lit up at the time?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that although he was not made privy to
  everything that transpired or know how Code Enforcement works
  within  their  capacity,  he  believes  that
  the signage was on and of course Code Enforcement in doing
  their due diligence, asked the applicant to turn off the
  signage, because they were not able to find an authorized
  sign adjustment permit, just the old pole design signed
  with the electronic sign.
 Is the sign animated or were the images still?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated the sign was on the issue was that it was
  an LED sign that was outside of the scope of what the IMC
  allows without the sign adjustment.
 Does staff know if this application is approved, will the
  displays be animated or still?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that per the applicant who is present,
  stated that if the sign is allowed to be utilized as is, it
  will have the display of the services that the business
  provides, finance and investments, current and past listings
  along with pictures of the listings from all over, not just
  Inglewood.
 Per the agenda packet, the applicant submitted a letter stating
  that an “eight-wheeled” vehicle parked would be large enough to
  block the sign as well as his business and he believes that the
  applicant is speaking about an “eighteen-wheeler” truck and was
  he correct in his summation of the applicant’s letter?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated yes that is correct, the applicant was
  meaning to say “eighteen wheeler”.

Commissioner Holly asked:
 If what the applicant is proposing similar to what is already
  displayed across town last year with another applicant in the
  City?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that although he is not aware of the other
  signage, this applicant is wanting to advertise other
  properties that are for sale which are not listed only in
  Inglewood, which would make the sign a completely different
  type of signage display that is not allowed per the IMC.

Commissioner Rice asked:
 In looking at the permit that was issued in May 2003 for the
  sign and that it should be a 6x9 Can, pole, with red neon
  borders, and excavation, which is a pole in the ground and also
  non-illuminated. Do you know if at any time the applicant
  changed the sign to show time, date and temperature?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that if in fact it was not approved under
  the original signage, then that would be a requirement.

Acting Chairman Coleman asked for the applicant to come forward
and address the planning commission.

Mr. Cole Feyijimi, owner made his presentation  and  answered
questions from the planning commission.

Commissioner Holly asked:
 Mr. Feyijimi, we would like to know why you did not do your due
  diligence and contact the planning division when you decided to
  change your original sign?
  - Mr. Feyijimi stated that he wasn’t sure what he was supposed
  to do with regards to obtaining a sign adjustment permit,
  since he had already received a sign permit in 2003. He felt

  3
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 6, 2019
  it was not necessary to obtain another permit since he already
  had the permit from 2003. The pole sign was already approved.

Commissioner Rice asked:
 Mr. Feyijimi, when and how did an eighteen wheeler block the
  pole sign and your business from being seen, when as high as
  the pole sign is, that seems a bit doubtful.
  - Mr. Feyijimi stated it is a true statement. One weekend, there
  was a driver who was staying at the hotel across the street
  and left his truck on our side of the street for the entire
  weekend, blocking our business with his truck.
 Mr. Feyijimi, who installed your pole sign without getting
  permits from the City?
  - Mr. Feyijimi stated that an acquaintance of his, knew a man
  who could make the sign, and so he contacted him. That
  gentleman made the pole sign back in 2003. So, when he made
  the decision to upgrade the sign, due to falling sales and
  trying to keep his business name present.
 Mr. Feyijimi, did you utilize a licensed contractor, was your
  associate’s friend a licensed contractor?
  - Mr. Feyijimi stated no, he did not have a license.
 Mr. Feyijimi, with your associate’s friend not having a license,
  this is what has brought you to this point, where you have a
  pole sign that cannot be approved due to the Municipal Code
  regulations.

Commissioner Trejo stated:
 Many days and evenings as she travels up and down Manchester
  Boulevard, she sees the pole sign from both near and far. The
  municipal code is in place for a reason.

Acting Chairman Coleman stated:
 He too has driven down Manchester Boulevard and immediately
  could see the pole sign from both near and far, and feels that
  it would be next to impossible to cover up the sign with an
  eighteen-wheeler.
 Mr. Feyijimi, before you were asked by Code Enforcement to
  darken your sign, was the pictures generated animated or still
  shots?
  - Mr. Feyijimi stated that the screen was animated.

Commissioner Rice asked staff:
 If Mr. Feyijimi returns the sign back to the original 2003
  approved pole sign, will he be able to utilize that for his
  sign?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that per the municipal code only what is
  approved is an illuminated sign that gives the date, time and
  hours of operation.

Acting Chairman Coleman opened the floor to the public to speak to
the planning commission for or against this item.

FOR:

Stuart Bailey, Inglewood Resident
  - Just a concerned citizen, but all is well.

AGAINST:

None

Acting-Chair Coleman asked for closing comments and also a motion
from the Planning Commission.

  4
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 6, 2019

MOTION:

Commissioner Trejo made the motion to affirm the notice of
exemption EA-CE-2018-099 and adopt the attached resolution
upholding the director’s denial of SA-2018-008 and was second by
Commissioner Rice, Resolution No. 1828,

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
  OF  THE  CITY  OF  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA,
  UPHOLDING THE DENIAL OF A CERTAIN SIGN
  ADJUSTMENT REQUEST TO LEGALIZE A PREVIOUSLY
  INSTALLED  APPROXIMATELY  48  SQUARE-FOOT
  INTERNALLY-ILLUMINATED BI-FACED LED SIGN FOR
  THE DISPLAY OF ON-SITE ADVERTISING ONLY ON
  APPROXIMATELY 3,700 SQUARE-FOOT C-2 (GENERAL
  COMMERCIAL) ZONED PROPERTY AT 532 WEST
  MANCHESTER BOULEVARD.

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners  Holly,  Rice,  Trejo,  and  Acting-Chair
  Coleman.

Ms. Wilcox explained there is no appeals process.

(6)  COMMISSION INITIATIVES:

Commissioner Holly no initiatives,  just  wanted  to  thank  the
community for coming out.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff about any update regarding the Hotel
Parking situation at the corner of Rosewood and Century Boulevard.
  - Ms. Wilcox stated she will have a response at next month’s
  planning commission meeting.

Acting-Chair Coleman asked staff about Michael Koper situation,
  - Ms. Wilcox stated she will have a response at next month’s
  planning commission meeting.

(7)  PUBLIC COMMENTS:

Mr. George Roblen, Inglewood Resident.
  - Concern of lack of parking in the City.

Ms. Sharon Mann-Garrett, Manager of Economic Development Division
  - Introduced herself to the Planning Commission and the
  community.
  - Explained her position with the community and here at the
  City.

  5
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 6, 2019

(8)  ADJOURNMENT:

Acting-Chair Coleman stated that he wanted to thank everyone for
and that he appreciated and thank you to all for attending
tonight’s Planning Commission meeting, and now this meeting is
adjourned at 7:43.

  _________________________________
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary
  City Planning Commission
  Inglewood, California
Approved this 4th Day
of September 2019.

___________________________
Acting-Chairman Terry Coleman
City Planning Commission

MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 4, 2019

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, September 4, 2019, in the
Community Room, on the first floor, in City Hall. Following the
Pledge of Allegiance by Commissioner Rice, the meeting was called
to order at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:

Present:  Commissioner Erick Holly
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aide’ Trejo
  Commissioner Terry Coleman
  Chairman Larry Springs

Staff:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Jeff Lewis, Assistant City Attorney
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Fred Jackson, Senior Planner
  Bernard McCrumby, Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner
  Taylor Kay, Assistant Planner
  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., Director of E.C.D.
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:

Ms. Wilcox stated that Item 6A has an edit change and a new draft
ordinance.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

None.

(5) MINUTES APPROVAL:

Commissioner Holly made the motion to approve the minutes of
February 6, 2019 and was seconded by Commissioner Coleman.

MOTION:

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Holly, Rice, Trejo, Coleman and Chairman
  Springs.

(6) PUBLIC HEARING:

6A. ZONING CODE AMENDMENT NO. 2019-001 (ZCA-2019-001) TO CHAPTER
12 C-S ZONE. A public hearing to consider Zoning Code Amendment
2019-001 (ZCA-2019-001) to Chapter 12 of the Inglewood Municipal
Code to allow towing service with ancillary vehicle storage and
ancillary vehicle inspection in the C-S (Commercial Service) zone
citywide.

Ms. Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner made the staff presentation.
Chairman Springs Larry asked the Planning Commission if there were
any questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice asked staff:
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 4, 2019

  Within the conditions, would there be any restrictions to the
  size or height of the vehicles? Also, there was no mention of
  boats, are there any or are they restricted or exempt? Also,
  are boats considered to be vehicles and would they be restricted
  also?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that boats would be within the category of
  trailers, due to being transported on trailers and trailers
  are not acceptable.
  Zoning Code Amendments in the C3 zone – What about storing of
  vehicles or towing services with ancillary storage?
  - Ms. Fewell stated no – towing service is not allowed in any
  of the zones within the city currently. Staff has historically
  categorized towing services as vehicle storage, and that
  designation is only allowed in the manufacturing zones.
  So this Zoning Code Amendment will help to clear or give these
  services a classification?
  - Ms. Fewell stated yes.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff:
 Would the Zoning Code Amendment open up additional locations
  for vehicle storage/towing?
  - Ms. Fewell stated it would allow the use of the CS Zone
  through special use permit approval.
 So currently, it is not allowed in the CS?
  - Ms. Fewell stated correct.
 So if this request is approved, the city would now allow more
  towing services in Inglewood, which would increase the sixteen
  already established towing services we have at present, correct?
  - Ms. Fewell stated correct.
 At present, vehicle storage which is allowed in the M-1 and M-
  2 zones is the only location where vehicle storage which
  basically means towing is allowed, correct?
  - Ms. Fewell stated correct.
 Why is this coming before the Planning Commission now to open
  up this CS zoned property for vehicle towing/storage services,
  which is already a very busy, heavily traveled corridor – was
  it because the applicant realized that the location where he
  wanted to conduct his business was not zoned for that use, and
  the only way he could have his business in that area would
  require the zone to be re-designated for the entire city to now
  allow vehicle towing/storage services?
  - Ms. Fewell stated correct.
 She asked staff to point-out on the map, all of the CS zones in
  the City, where on the map the location of the new business and
  what areas would the zoned area change effect the city with the
  new designation.
  - Ms. Fewell stated that the various areas of the city that
  would be effected would include La Brea Boulevard starting at
  Spruce Avenue and heading south on La Brea/Hawthorne
  Boulevard to 104th Street or the city boundary.
 Then she stated with the approval of this zone change it would
  open the main corridor of the city to be over-run with even more
  auto-related businesses and services, also allowing very
  unpleasing landscapes of six-foot high fencing not very
  esthetically pleasing to the eye and take away from the enhanced
  spatial experience which is where this city is going toward
  improving everything that we possibly can. Several of our
  neighboring communities have enhanced their landscaping, also
  cleaning up a lot of businesses and their main street
  thoroughfares such as Lennox, Hawthorne, Lawndale and Torrance.

  2
   Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
  September 4, 2019

    She also stated that the City of Inglewood has sixteen like
  businesses already within a nine square-foot mile City. The
  appropriate location for these types of businesses would be in
  the M-1 & M-2 zones.

  Chairman Springs asked Commissioner Trejo if she would possibly
  save any further questions for the applicant, and she stated that
  she would do so.

  Commissioner Coleman asked –
   Say an applicant receives an approval for a towing yard on the
  CS corridor and then six months later applies for another
  approval for a like business, and applies for another – does
  the applicant have to return to the city and come before the
  planning commission to request approval again and again each
  time or does the applicant have a cart blanche’ authorization
  and only has to apply once? How does it work?
  - Ms. Fewell stated the city is recommending first the special
  use permit approval, so each new towing business that comes
  into the CS zone, must obtain an approval through an SUP.
  Then there is a business requirement of 1,000 foot separation
  between an active towing business and then the new request
  coming in. In general, the 1,000 feet separation would equal
  typically two mega(super) blocks.

  Commissioner Rice asked staff:
   Would the separation between businesses apply to both sides of
  the street, if there was an approved towing business in the CS
  zone would that apply to the opposite side of the street or is
  it just linear distance? Is the map being used this evening for
  demonstrative purposes only, whereas the CS zone actually goes
  further, starting at Florence Boulevard all the way south to
  104th Street – actually the city’s border to border?
  - Ms. Fewell stated – it would be on both sides – property to
  property. This map is pulled from the City’s GIS Dept., this
  is the actual live map, and the distance covers from Spruce
  to 104th Street.

  Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward and address
  the planning commission.

  Mr. Robert Rudolph, representative for the applicant, and Mr.
  Robert Van Langen, Employee; addressed the planning commission.

  Chairman Springs opened the floor for questions to the applicants
  by the planning commission.

  Commissioner Holly asked –
   Just two questions – the first, where is your subject site
  located presently (asking staff to show the GIS map for visual)?
  - Mr. Rudolph stated they were located just one block south of
  Century Boulevard, on 102nd Street and Hawthorne Boulevard,
  on the west side of the street.
   In the staff report, it states “with ancillary vehicle
  inspections”, for clarification explain what does “with
  ancillary vehicle inspections” entail?
-  Mr. Rudolph stated that it could be for impound or a police request
  most of the time, generally all the time. And that car is held u

  3
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 4, 2019

Commissioner Rice stated:
 His question is for staff first, will this project site be up
  for design review? Will staff require a six-foot enclosed
  landscaped wall for compliance?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated no regarding Design Review at the planning
  commission level, but yes at the staff level for this project.
  - Mr. Rudolph stated that they will be working with staff to
  insure that they comply with all landscaping requirements and
  directions for beautification of our wall, and they will
  comply with the enclosed six-foot wall.

Commissioner Trejo stated:
 That this request is not for just one tow service application
  or business, but for opening the entire corridor for multiple
  tow services - if this action is approved.
 Then she asked Mr. Rudolph about the fact that they have been
  at this present location which is a CS Zone location for over
  1-yr., when they attempted to acquire their business license
  and found out that this location could not be used for this type
  of business, what happened next?
  - Mr. Rudolph stated that they were in the process of having a
  contractor assist them with some remodeling and there was
  some misunderstanding all around, so when they attempted to
  secure the garage with some better doors and in attempting to
  make the garage facility area stronger, that’s when we learned
  at that time through the field inspector that there was an
  issue with us being at this site.
 She stated that with this information the applicant went to
  obtain a business license, but could not without having to
  change the entire CS Zone corridor to allow for this type of
  location, but multiple areas and sites in the City.
 She then asked Mr. Reynolds how many vehicles can be stored on
  a 30,000+ square foot property.
  - Mr. Reynolds stated that it is over 30,000 square feet, and
  the storage capacity is about 80 to 100 cars, he would have
  to consult with his staff for the actual numbers, if he could
  do that right now… And, how many tow trucks at the site?
  - Mr. Robert Van Langen of B&H Tow, stated that if all the
  vehicles are packed in tightly, there is the potential of 200
  cars, but that is regulation, and at present we have 77
  vehicles on the lot, generally we run between 60 to 79 cars
  with 12 Tow Trucks on site.
 She also stated that with using the range of 60-79 cars and the
  12 trucks, the applicant’s lot will have a possible 90 vehicles
  on site. She then asked staff what are the requirements for tow
  service allotment of vehicles and parking lot requirements for
  improvement’s and maintenance on a site? Would it be specific
  to this applicant’s tow service or is there a general blanket
  requirement to obtain a Special Use Permit for this CS zone?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that yes this applicant would be subject to
  the City’s parking lot improvement requirements essentially
  require a 3.5 foot half wall and a landscaping buffer around
  parking lots with lighting and amenities along those lines,
  to be included. The way the CS zone code amendment has been
  drafted would require a 6-foot high screen wall around the
  storage areas of the site, but not the general parking areas.
  In those general areas, the parking lot improvements of the
  3.5 foot wall would be in effect. Also note that the code as
  currently written, allows for a commercial property to build
  a 6-foot high wall along their property line with a landscaped
  buffer, and this proposed code amendment is written to require
  a six-foot high screening wall around the storage areas.
  4
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 4, 2019

Commissioner Coleman asked:
 If a constituent has been towed after a long evening of enjoying
  the city’s events with Hollywood Park and maybe at the Forum,
  etc., and finds that their vehicle has been towed to this site,
  will there be staff available 24 hours who can assist with the
  retrieving of that constituent’s vehicle? Per the staff report,
  you state that you will have the office opened only from 7:00am
  until 10:00pm.
  - Mr. Reynolds stated that there will be a staff person at the
  office to inform the tow truck driver on duty that there is
  an customer at the office attempting to do a pick-up of their
  vehicle that has been deposited in the tow yard, then staff
  would inform the customer that the tow truck driver is out at
  a location, and once he has completed his task, he will return
